frontier.hypothesis: Inserting build/src/text1b.o(.rodata) at exactly 0x80015988 (moved from bb2.ld:66), deleting jtbl_80015988 from src/text1a_b_pre_rodata.c and splitting that TU so D_800159A0 onward follows text1b.o, with candidate.c applied to src/text1b.c, makes the full build SHA1-match.
frontier.mechanism: Session 9 certified both remaining preconditions at byte level: our emitted table relocates to the target's six words exactly (uniform base 0x80062164), and the 24-byte hole at 0x80015988 absorbs our 8-aligned section with zero padding on either side.
frontier.next_probe: Requires atomic edits to bb2.ld plus a second src file, outside a grind session's surface — an operator or multi-file-authorized session applies the 2026-09-16 integration-handoff steps in docs/grind/decisions.md and certifies with verify-oracle --rebuild (SHA1), not the sandbox score (pinned at 2 by construction).

frontier.hypothesis: Listing jtbl_80015988 in LD_SYM_FILES would let the sandbox resolve the symbol and certify the body without a full build.
frontier.mechanism: engine/score.py:62 resolves named-symbol HI16/LO16 pairs against LD_SYM_FILES addresses; jtbl_80015988 is unlisted because the rodata cleanup made it a C const.
frontier.next_probe: named_syms.txt is a build-pipeline file outside a grind session's surface; needs an operator decision or ruling before measuring.

frontier.hypothesis: Decompiling func_80065800 (owner of jtbl_80015940, the symbol immediately before ours) in the same pass would let both tables be emitted by text1b.o in ascending order, collapsing part of the pre/post split.
frontier.mechanism: GCC emits switch tables in the order their switch statements appear in the TU; func_80065800 is an active sibling in the same file.
frontier.next_probe: Out of scope for a single-function session; a session handed func_80065800 should re-derive the slot boundary from evidence.md Sessions 7b/9 before proposing a placement.
